carrier_signals: visible poster edge or mounting logic
layout_select_when: An editorial poster must carry 5–7 truthful text elements such as a title, deck, date, location, index, classification, or footer.
layout_dominant_mass: title remains first; factual support copy becomes the structural skeleton
layout_forbidden_relationships: support copy detached from the information rule
equal hierarchy between title and factual clusters
layout_title_zone: one large block intersecting or sharing a rule with the factual system
layout_object_slot: one specimen, fragment, or counterweight attached to the same rule or grid
layout_collision_rule: headline, object, and facts share one explicit axis; rules organize information rather than decorate the page
layout_crop_rule: the subject may crop against the information axis; text never crops and factual strings remain legible
layout_required_structure: one primary information rule or grid
one subject attached to the same system
layout_failure_signals: decorative rules with no alignment job
layout_thumbnail_test: the title reads first, the information axis reads second, and the support copy collapses into one coherent system
subject_assembly_count: one coherent subject, object, image field, or abstract field
subject_mass_rule: Treat the single subject as one complete, cropped, fragmented, or field-like mass according to the Composition Contract.

composition_operators.definition: Attach title, subject, and truthful factual support to one explicit rule, grid, or index axis.
Attach at least three major or support elements to one shared edge, axis, baseline, or curvature.
Protect one open band or corner from subjects so title and facts remain readable.
Make the title approach, split around, or track one meaningful subject contour while preserving glyph clarity.

composition_sentence: TITLE_MASS + SINGLE_OBJECT + INFORMATION_RULE + CONTOUR_LOCK + RELEASE_ZONE + SHARED_ALIGNMENT
subject_origin_definition: A recognizable object from the real technological past, treated as historical evidence rather than redesigned as a generic future prop.
subject_identity_contract: preserve original proportions and 2–4 category-defining parts
retain readable distinctions between materials such as aged plastic, glass, metal, rubber, paper, and screen
allow environmental tint and print grain, but do not recolor or smooth the artifact until its historical provenance disappears
preserve authentic labels or interface text when identity-bearing and non-dominant; never invent replacement labels
render_treatment_definition: Preserve local object color, material evidence, and product separation; let the palette surround and support the subject.
render_color_rule: Original local colors remain identifiable. Environmental color may appear in shadows and highlights but cannot become the object's new base color.
scale_role_behavior: Show the object complete or nearly complete as a central product or archival exhibit; use title and support copy to frame it.
screen_state_definition: The selected subject has no generated screen behavior.
screen_rendering_rule: Do not add a display, interface, glow, or control surface merely to make the subject look technological.
intrinsic_artifact_text_policy: It is not designed poster copy and is not automatically cropped. Preserve it when identity-bearing and safe; keep it subordinate and never replace it with invented legible text. Hide or soften it only when it competes with the title, contains sensitive or unsuitable information, or cannot be rendered faithfully. Generated SCREEN_CARRIER copy is explicitly excluded: it remains designed copy and counts toward the carrier text budget.
focal_event: The title approaches, splits around, or tracks one outer contour of the primary form.
release_zone: the quiet side of the form and any unused space beside short title lines
focal_event_thumbnail_test: title reads as one dominant block, not scattered labels
derived_tints: derive pale, mid, and soft-deep tones only from the active hues
saturation_rule: allow only one saturation focus; render all other hues as softened fields, haze, or translucent layers
gradient_direction: diffuse light spreads along an asymmetric soft horizon
primary_form: one coherent media component, media stack, or object-plus-medium relationship with historically plausible proportions
primary_form_placement: authoritative layout object slot: one specimen, fragment, or counterweight attached to the same rule or grid; adapt the object's preferred placement cue (large centered advertising hero) inside that slot rather than replacing it; use the locked title relationship: rainbow or rule bridges title and device; apply crop rule: the subject may crop against the information axis; text never crops and factual strings remain legible; apply scale role CENTERPIECE_ARTIFACT: Show the object complete or nearly complete as a central product or archival exhibit; use title and support copy to frame it.; resolve SUBJECT_ASSEMBLY SINGLE_OBJECT: Treat the single subject as one complete, cropped, fragmented, or field-like mass according to the Composition Contract.

hero_object.geometry: one coherent media component, media stack, or object-plus-medium relationship with historically plausible proportions
hero_object.material: retain real plastic, brushed metal, glass, printed controls, cassette windows, paper labels, and wear without inventing legible copy; render treatment FAITHFUL_RETAINED: Plastic, glass, metal, rubber, screen, and paper remain visibly distinct.
hero_object.lighting: warm catalog light, flat print-ad lighting, or softly graded archival photography
hero_object.placement: authoritative layout object slot: one specimen, fragment, or counterweight attached to the same rule or grid; adapt the object's preferred placement cue (large centered advertising hero) inside that slot rather than replacing it; use the locked title relationship: rainbow or rule bridges title and device; apply crop rule: the subject may crop against the information axis; text never crops and factual strings remain legible; apply scale role CENTERPIECE_ARTIFACT: Show the object complete or nearly complete as a central product or archival exhibit; use title and support copy to frame it.; resolve SUBJECT_ASSEMBLY SINGLE_OBJECT: Treat the single subject as one complete, cropped, fragmented, or field-like mass according to the Composition Contract.
hero_object.title_relationship: use the object's selected placement and keep its identity anchors outside the title clear zone
identity_anchors: period-correct screen, tape door, disc tray, or disk shell
recognizable transport controls, knobs, or meter field
stacked component proportions or one clear media slot
aged plastic, brushed metal, glass, and cable separation
hero_object.visual_behavior: treat controls and media slots as material evidence, not decorative interface noise
hero_object.function_requirement: preserve the object's real historical function and provenance
hero_object.screen_rendering_rule: Do not add a display, interface, glow, or control surface merely to make the subject look technological.
hero_object.role_scale_rule: Show the object complete or nearly complete as a central product or archival exhibit; use title and support copy to frame it. The object owns the focal scale; supporting accents remain flat and subordinate.
hero_object.subject_mass_rule: Treat the single subject as one complete, cropped, fragmented, or field-like mass according to the Composition Contract.

spatial_assignment: obey the layout collision rule: headline, object, and facts share one explicit axis; rules organize information rather than decorate the page Distribute visual weight before establishing alignment; do not concentrate the title, hero, and decorative axis on one side unless the opposite region has a clear compositional role
title_clear_zone: the union of visible title glyph silhouettes plus a calm buffer of about 4% of canvas width; the primary form's solid silhouette, luminous core, and highest-contrast edge must stay outside it; soft low-contrast atmosphere may pass behind only when glyph edges and thumbnail readability remain crisp
primary_form_clearance: CATEGORY_LABEL outlines, ANCHOR, ECHO, and decorative lines must not cross the primary form's core contour, highest-contrast region, or visual center; place them along an outer edge, tangent, or extended axis instead
collision_resolution: preserve approved wording and readable title scale; use balanced reflow when suitable, otherwise translate or modestly scale the primary form; never preserve centered placement at the cost of glyph clearance
detail_limits: one accent language plus at most one hairline bridge; accents under 2% combined canvas area
detail_grammar: one ANCHOR, zero or one BRIDGE, and one or two ECHO instances using one returned accent language
alignment_system: first distribute visual weight across complementary regions, then align at least three of title, hero or atmospheric form, panel, label, bridge, and accents through a shared edge, axis, tangent, baseline, or curvature; the relationship may span the canvas and must not stack all high-information elements in one region
